text: Question: Which of the following medical asepsis actions should the nurse take to reduce and prevent the spread of microorganisms? Select all that apply.
A. Practicing hand hygiene.
B. Reapplying a sterile dressing.
C. Sterilizing contaminating items.
D. Applying a sterile gown and gloves.
E. Routinely cleaning the hospital environment.
F. Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body fluids.
Correct answers: A. Practicing hand hygiene.; E. Routinely cleaning the hospital environment.; F. Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body fluids.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Practicing hand hygiene” – This is not a sterile procedure.
• “Routinely cleaning the hospital environment” – This is not a sterile procedure.
• “Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body flu…” – This is not a sterile procedure.
Not correct:
• “Reapplying a sterile dressing” – This is a sterile procedure.
• “Sterilizing contaminating items” – This is a sterile procedure.
• “Applying a sterile gown and gloves” – This is a sterile procedure.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with a decubitus ulcer (stage 4). The wound culture result shows MRSA in the wound bed. Which type of transmission-based precautions should the nurse institute?
A. Standard.
B. Droplet.
C. Contact.
D. Airborne.
Correct answer: C. Contact.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Contact” – MRSA in a wound indicates contact isolation.
Not correct:
• “Standard” – Although they are used for all clients, standard precautions would not help decrease the spread of MRSA.
• “Droplet” – MRSA in the nares would indicate droplet isolation.
• “Airborne” – This isolation is indicated for very small molecules that linger for long periods in the air.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse is triaging clients involved in a mass causality disaster using the co
text: Question: The nurse is triaging clients involved in a mass causality disaster using the color-coded tagging system. Which clients should be tagged red? Select all that apply.
A. Is deceased.
B. Has chest pain.
C. Has a leg sprain.
D. Has a chest wound.
E. Has multiple closed fractures.
F. Has full thickness burns over 30% of the body.
Correct answers: B. Has chest pain.; D. Has a chest wound.; F. Has full thickness burns over 30% of the body.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Has chest pain” – This client would be in the red category.
• “Has a chest wound” – This client would be in the red category.
• “Has full thickness burns over 30% of the body” – This client would be red since they have less then 65% burns on their body.
Not correct:
• “Is deceased” – This client would be in the black category.
• “Has a leg sprain” – This client would be in the green category.
• “Has multiple closed fractures” – This client would be in the yellow category.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The charge nurse observes a newly hired nurse caring for a client with a wrist r
text: Question: The charge nurse observes a newly hired nurse caring for a client with a wrist restraint. Which of the following observations by the charge nurse requires follow up with the newly hired nurse?
A. A safety knot was used to secure the restraint.
B. The call light was placed within reach of the client.
C. The restraint was applied tightly around the client's wrist.
D. The clients record indicates that the restraint was released every 2 hours.
Correct answer: C. The restraint was applied tightly around the client's wrist.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “The restraint was applied tightly around the client's wrist” – The client's restraints should not be tight.
Not correct:
• “A safety knot was used to secure the restraint” – This is the correct type of knot to use.
• “The call light was placed within reach of the client” – This is correct for safety.
• “The clients record indicates that the restraint was released every 2…” – This is the correct amount of time that restraints should be released for ROM.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: The nurse is discussing accident prevention with the family of an older client who is being discharged following hip surgery. Which of the following physical factors place the client at risk for injury in the home? Select all that apply.
A. A night light in the bathroom.
B. Elevated toilet seat with armrests.
C. Cooking equipment (ex. stove).
D. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors.
E. A low thermostat setting on the water heater.
F. Common household objects such as a doormat or rug.
Correct answers: C. Cooking equipment (ex. stove).; F. Common household objects such as a doormat or rug.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Cooking equipment (ex. stove)” – The client could burn themselves if they fall.
• “Common household objects such as a doormat or rug” – The client could fall.
Not correct:
• “A night light in the bathroom” – This is safe.
• “Elevated toilet seat with armrests” – This is safe.
• “Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors” – This is safe.
• “A low thermostat setting on the water heater” – This is safe.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse preceptor is describing critical pathways and variance analysis to a n
text: Question: The nurse preceptor is describing critical pathways and variance analysis to a new graduate. The preceptor explains that a variance analysis is preformed on all clients with respect to which time frame?
A. Continuously.
B. Daily.
C. Every third day.
D. Every other day.
Correct answer: A. Continuously.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Continuously” – It is an ongoing process.
Not correct:
• “Daily”
• “Every third day”
• “Every other day”
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse is teaching a client with cardiomyopathy about safety measures when at
text: Question: The nurse is teaching a client with cardiomyopathy about safety measures when at home. Which of the following instructions is most important?
A. Reporting pain.
B. Taking a vasodilator.
C. Avoid over the counter medications.
D. Moving slowly from a sitting to a standing position.
Correct answer: D. Moving slowly from a sitting to a standing position.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Moving slowly from a sitting to a standing position” – Moving fast could result in orthostatic hypotension and the client would fall.
Not correct:
• “Reporting pain” – This is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
• “Taking a vasodilator” – This is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
• “Avoid over the counter medications” – This is important to educate but does not relate directly to safety.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse is assigning clients to a LPN/LVN and UAP. Which clients should the nu
text: Question: The nurse is assigning clients to a LPN/LVN and UAP. Which clients should the nurse assign to the LPN/LVN? Select all that apply
A. A client needing frequent suctioning.
B. A client requiring a dressing change to the foot.
C. A client requiring passive range of motion exercises twice daily.
D. A client requiring reinforcement of teaching about a diabetic diet.
E. A client requiring vital signs every 8 hours.
Correct answers: A. A client needing frequent suctioning.; B. A client requiring a dressing change to the foot.; D. A client requiring reinforcement of teaching about a diabetic diet.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “A client needing frequent suctioning.” – Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
• “A client requiring a dressing change to the foot.” – Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
• “A client requiring reinforcement of teaching about a diabetic diet.” – Yes, this is under the LPN scope of practice.
Not correct:
• “A client requiring passive range of motion exercises twice daily.” – No, this can be done by the UAP.
• “A client requiring vital signs every 8 hours.” – No, this can be done by the UAP.
(Copied from the class slide answer page: live review rn safety infection pre, slide 32.)

text: Question: Which of the following actions should the nurse take when caring for a client with accidental poisoning? Select all that apply.
A. Save vomitus for laboratory analysis.
B. Place the client in a supine position.
C. Induce vomiting if a household cleaner was ingested.
D. Assess for airway patency, breathing, and circulation.
E. Determine the type and amount of substance ingested.
F. Remove any visible materials from the nose and mouth.

Correct answers: A. Save vomitus for laboratory analysis.; D. Assess for airway patency, breathing, and circulation.; E. Determine the type and amount of substance ingested.; F. Remove any visible materials from the nose and mouth.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Save vomitus for laboratory analysis” – This is correct.
• “Assess for airway patency, breathing, and circulation” – This is correct.
• “Determine the type and amount of substance ingested” – This is correct.
• “Remove any visible materials from the nose and mouth” – This is correct.
Not correct:
• “Place the client in a supine position” – This could result in aspiration pneumonia.
• “Induce vomiting if a household cleaner was ingested” – This would cause the esophagus to suffer burns twice.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: A nurse is working with an emergency response team in caring for a group of people who may have been exposed to anthrax while doing farm work but are not exhibiting manifestation of illness. Select three prescriptions that the nurse would anticipate receiving from the primary health care provider (PHCP).
A. Ciprofloxacin.
B. Propranolol.
C. Hydroxychloroquine.
D. Furosemide.
E. Doxycycline.
F. Clindamycin.
Correct answers: A. Ciprofloxacin.; E. Doxycycline.; F. Clindamycin.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:

Antibiotics are used for anthrax exposure. Ciprofloxacin and doxycycline are the first-line choices and clindamycin is also used in anthrax regimens. Propranolol, hydroxychloroquine, and furosemide do not treat anthrax. Confirm the exact regimen against your class notes.
